findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The PIC during the inspection was unable to provide a current CFPM certificate during the inspection. The inspector tried to walk them through finding the copy they said they had online but they could not remember which company they received it from. They also stated that the current people with manager certificates were themselves and one other. A hand out was given during the inspection for the local CFPM courses/tests in the area. Ensure that there is always a CFPM available at the facility at all times that foods or food contact items are being handled.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the two sani buckets in the facility were observed low on the inspector’s test strips. The facility made new buckets of sanitizer to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers are at effective levels at all times while in use at the facility.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 6-201.16(A) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE.

Acoustic type ceiling tiles are observed in the bathrooms. Ceiling coverings should be smooth and easily cleanable. The locations were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to replace prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. 

The kit intended for clean-up of vomit/diarrheal events is missing the chemical needed for disinfection of the affected area. The PIC was consulted and quickly ran to the store in order to acquire bleach for this procedure. They also stated that a new kit will be purchased/ordered for future use. They returned with the bleach during this inspection and was walked through its use in relation to these procedure. Ensure that the procedures needed for these events have all needed supplies available at all times moving forward.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure.

An employee was observed to wash hands and then use their bare hand to actuate the paper towel dispenser, recontaminating their hands. Food service began directly after this event was observed. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to ensure that all food handlers properly wash their hands prior to food service, and that the hand washing procedures do not allow for re-contamination of the hands prior to food handling practices.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

No CFPM was available at the facility on inspector’s arrival. The manager arrived during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that enough CFPMs are on staff so that one is on site at all times of operation.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee was observed to wash hands and then use their bare hand to turn off the faucet prior to grabbing a paper towel. Education was conducted with the PIC. They are instructed to educate employees and ensure proper hand washing techniques are used.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: No Certified Food Manager present at time of inspection. Ensure sufficient staff have completed CFM course to cover all shifts of food prep and service.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Single service paper cookie sleeves observed stored below the handwashing sink. Store single service/food contact items where they are protected from potential contamination. Relocate so that they are not below the handwashing sink where they may be subject to leaks.
4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
No Certified Food Manager present at time of inspection. Ensure sufficient staff have completed CFM course to cover all shifts of food prep and service.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employee observed picking something up off the floor (from a pile of waste), donning gloves, and handling food without washing hands. Wash hands after any task that may have contaminated hands. CORRECTED-- Discussed handwashing with PIC and employee and provided education.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
No paper towels present in the womens restroom. CORRECTED-- Paper towels provided.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Meatballs observed to be 104F (probed) in the hot holding unit. Ensure hot held foods are maintained 135F or above. CORRECTED-- Meatballs voluntarily discarded.
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Neither of the two employees present have completed food handler training despite having been employed at the facility for more than 30 days. Staff must complete food handler training.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed customer soda fountain nozzles to have an accumulation of slime. CORRECTED- PIC will clean and sanitize soda nozzles. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned and sanitized as often as necessary to prevent soil build-up.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. (Pf)

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment: Observed flies throughout the kitchen, mainly in the back kitchen and storage areas.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES. (C)
See 6-202.13 in the 2017 FDA Food Code for information on food-safe pest control methods.
